summary: Notes by Richard Watson on a phone call with Bob Kahn about the ICCC network demonstration. They cover the physical setup in a hotel ballroom, including a false floor, a partition for a movie on resource sharing, and tables instead of booths. Other practical questions are covered too.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 372 records a conversation about plans for an ARPANET demonstration at the ICCC. It covers the room setup, equipment, participating groups, testing and visitor information.

subtitle: Planning notes for the ARPANET demonstration at the ICCC

tldr.problem: The ICCC network demonstration required coordination of space, equipment, participants and visitor support.
tldr.mechanism: Richard Watson records a conversation with Bob Kahn about the planned ballroom setup, demonstrations, testing and documentation.
tldr.outcome: The notes capture plans and unresolved arrangements for the October conference demonstration.

today: RFC 372 is a planning record for the ICCC network demonstration. It describes arrangements and questions as they stood during the conversation recorded in July 1972.

sections.title: A Conversation About the Demonstration
sections.content: Richard Watson of SRI-ARC wrote notes from a telephone conversation with Bob Kahn about the ICCC network demonstration. The conversation covered the physical space, staffing, equipment, demonstrations and preparations for visitors.
sections.plainLanguage: Watson wrote down what he and Kahn discussed about organizing the network demonstration. The notes include both settled arrangements and items that still needed work.

sections.title: Room, Equipment and Testing
sections.content:
The planned venue was the Georgetown Ballroom at the Hilton Hotel. The proposed layout used tables with terminals and partitions rather than conventional booths, with a separate area for a movie about resource sharing. Kahn expected testing of terminals and network resources before the event, including checks of how terminals worked with particular resources.

The notes say the TIP had not yet been tested with 64 terminals.
sections.plainLanguage: The organizers planned tables with terminals, a movie area and tests before the conference. They had not yet tested the TIP with 64 terminals.

sections.title: Demonstrations and Visitor Support
sections.content: The notes list possible demonstrations from network sites, including network measurement, artificial intelligence, mathematical software, natural-language programs and data management. Some commitments were still uncertain. The organizers also discussed staffing terminals with people who could demonstrate programs and answer visitors' questions.
sections.plainLanguage: Several sites were preparing programs to demonstrate. The organizers also wanted people available to explain the equipment and help visitors use it.

sections.title: Signs and Documentation
sections.content: Plans for visitor guidance included signs, a card listing TIP commands and resources, a brochure with example uses, a movie and people on the floor who could help. Watson and Kahn discussed coordinating these materials with NIC documentation. Watson also notes that the show had no separate ARPA budget beyond contributions contractors might make through ongoing research.
sections.plainLanguage: The organizers planned signs, printed instructions and staff to explain the demonstrations. The notes say funding depended on contributions from ongoing work.
